11.2a — Create PT: Video + PPR

Production day. Two artifacts leave this room as part of your AP score: the video (behavior, demonstrated by you, under 60 seconds) and the Personalized Project Reference — the PPR — the ONLY notes you may hold while answering WR2 on exam day. Both are made today.

Record ~25 min

Video rules (read twice, then rehearse once more):

  • Under 60 continuous seconds, one take (edits are forbidden — one unbroken recording)
  • Must show: input happening, program behavior, output — your 11.1d demo path
  • Voiceover or on-screen text explaining purpose; your face is optional, your program is not
  • No names of classmates or school (privacy rule)

Recording ritual: stopwatch rehearsal → recording one → watch it → one fix if needed → recording two, done. Retaking forever is a trap; your demo path is already rehearsed. Save as MP4 and back it up in TWO places (repo folder + cloud).

The PPR (the exam-day cheat sheet you write yourself): a PDF of up to 5 program components:

  1. Your list declaration (the real line)
  2. The procedure with parameters (the real signature)
  3. The algorithm body (the real code with your three S/S/I parts visible)
  4. A call site (the real call)
  5. One more: the input handler or the output line

That PPR prints with you into the exam room on May 14 — WR2a/2b/2c are answered FROM IT. Screenshot the exact lines, not from memory.

Bug Hunt: Submission-blockers

  1. Your video shows the Unity editor with your school's name in the window title. What does the privacy rule say — and what is the 5-second fix (crop / rename)?
  2. The video is 61 seconds. What gets cut — and why is it ALWAYS the waiting between inputs, never the input or the output?
  3. Your PPR has "cleaned-up" code that differs from the video's behavior. Why must PPR and video MATCH exactly (the grader cross-references them)?
Close of Day ~5 min

Tinker: Deliverables

  1. Both files exist, named and backed up: video.mp4 + PPR.pdf in the repo folder.
  2. Commit + push: "11.2a: video + PPR".

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Show a sub-60s one-take video demonstrating input → behavior → output
  • Show a PPR with real code excerpts, matching the video
  • Explain the PPR's exam-day role (WR2's only notes)
  • Have both files backed up in two places
